# The Emergency, 1975-77

<!-- STEP id="early-1970s" -->
## The Early 1970s

One of the major challenges to democracy in India came in 1975-77. In the early 1970s, public dissatisfaction with the government led by Indira Gandhi was growing. Rising unemployment, inflation and allegations of misgovernance led to widespread protests.

<!-- STEP id="movements" -->
## Mass Movements

In these years, mass movements led by Jayaprakash Narayan mobilised students and citizens, especially in Bihar and Gujarat. He was a political leader and socialist thinker, popularly known as Lok Nayak.

<!-- STEP id="june-1975" -->
## June 1975

In June 1975, a National Emergency was imposed by the government on the grounds of internal disturbance.

Articles 352, 356 and 360 deal with National Emergency, President's Rule and Financial Emergency.

<!-- STEP id="during" -->
## During This Period

During this period, a majority of Fundamental Rights were suspended, the press was censored, and numerous political leaders and activists were arrested.

Democratic institutions came under severe strain, and citizens' freedom was restricted.
